items.informal_name: Natural Degree of $ p \cdot X^n $ Equals $ \deg(p) + n $
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] [Nontrivial R] {p : Polynomial R} (n : ℕ),
  p ≠ 0 → (p * Polynomial.X ^ n).natDegree = p.natDegree + n
items.informal_description: For any non-zero polynomial $ p $ over a semiring $ R $ and any natural number $ n $, the natural degree of the product $ p \cdot X^n $ is equal to the natural degree of $ p $ plus $ n $. This follows from the definition of polynomial multiplication, where multiplying by $ X^n $ shifts all terms of $ p $ upward by $ n $ degrees, increasing the leading term's degree accordingly.

items.informal_name: Natural Degree of $X^n \cdot p$ Equals $\operatorname{nat-degree}(p) + n$
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] [Nontrivial R] {p : Polynomial R} (n : ℕ),
  p ≠ 0 → (Polynomial.X ^ n * p).natDegree = p.natDegree + n
items.informal_description: For any non-zero polynomial $p \in R[X]$ and natural number $n$, the natural degree of the product $X^n \cdot p$ satisfies $\operatorname{nat-degree}(X^n \cdot p) = \operatorname{nat-degree}(p) + n$.

items.informal_name: Natural Degree of $ p \cdot X $ is $ \operatorname{natdeg}(p) + 1 $
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] [Nontrivial R] {p : Polynomial R},
  p ≠ 0 → (p * Polynomial.X).natDegree = p.natDegree + 1
items.informal_description: For any non-zero polynomial $ p $ over a semiring $ R $, the natural degree of the product $ p \cdot X $ (where $ X $ is the indeterminate) is equal to the natural degree of $ p $ plus one. This follows from the definition of polynomial multiplication, where multiplying by $ X $ increases the degree of each term by one.

items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] [Nontrivial R] {p : Polynomial R},
  p ≠ 0 → (Polynomial.X * p).natDegree = p.natDegree + 1
items.informal_description: For any non-zero polynomial $ p $ over a semiring $ R $, the natural degree of $ X \cdot p $ is equal to the natural degree of $ p $ plus one, i.e., $ \natdegree(Xp) = \natdegree(p) + 1 $.

items.informal_name: Natural Degree of $ C(a) \cdot X^n $ is $ n $
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] (n : ℕ) (a : R), a ≠ 0 → (Polynomial.C a * Polynomial.X ^ n).natDegree = n
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n$ and non-zero element $a$ in a semiring $R$, the natural degree of the polynomial $C(a) \cdot X^n$ (where $C(a)$ denotes the constant polynomial embedding of $a$) is equal to $n$.

items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] [Nontrivial R] {p : Polynomial R} (n : ℕ),
  (p * Polynomial.X ^ n).degree = p.degree + ↑n
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ over a semiring and natural number $ n $, the degree of the product $ p \cdot X^n $ is equal to the sum of the degree of $ p $ and $ n $. This follows from the definition of polynomial multiplication, where multiplying by $ X^n $ shifts all exponents in $ p $ by $ n $, thereby increasing the maximum degree by $ n $.
